edition.locus: De Fabrica Mundi sixth day / image-likeness
edition.license: Public domain (Migne PL 5; Routh Reliquiae Sacrae III 451)
edition.note: Continuous sixth-day lock follows printed Migne/Routh column, not Walker conjectures as base text.

source_text: Die quinto terra et aqua foetus suos ediderunt. Die sexto creata sunt, quae deerant; ac sic Deus hominem de humo instruxit, dominum omnium rerum, quae super terram et super aquam creavit. Prius tamen angelos atque archangelos creavit, quam hominem finxit, spiritalia terrenis anteponens. Prius enim lux, quam coelum et terram. Hic dies sextus parasceve appellatur, praeparatio scilicet regni; Adam enim quem ad imaginem et similitudinem suam consummavit. Idcirco autem prius opera sua consummavit, quam angelos creavit, et hominem fabricavit, ne forte adjutores se fuisse falsa dictione asseverant.
pass_a_gloss: Fifth/sixth day; human from soil; angels before man; light before heaven/earth; parasceve; Adam completed in image/likeness; finished works so none claim to be helpers.
pass_b_english: On the fifth day land and water brought forth their young. On the sixth day the things still lacking were created; and so God formed the human being from the soil as lord of all he had made on land and water. Yet he created angels and archangels before he fashioned the human, putting spiritual things before earthly ones. For light was before heaven and earth. This sixth day is called parasceve — preparation of the kingdom. He completed Adam after his image and likeness. For that reason he finished his works before he created the angels and fashioned the human, lest they falsely claim they had been his helpers.

anf_compare.notes: Sense matches ANF sixth-day paragraph including light-before-heaven; removed invented free-choice gloss.

variants.note: Walker/Routh apparatus: four words transposed vs MS before “die sexto”; printed column follows Walker’s restored order.
Walker: forte terra for “coelum et terram”; deletes quem; forte asseverarent for printed asseverant/adseverant.
Traditional double clause kept: angels-before-man AND finished-works-before-angels-and-man (anti-helper).
